three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-22-5p in isomiRdb is −1 nt (46% of reads, pooled), against 36% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 66% of hsa-miR-22-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 55%–84%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 66% of hsa-miR-22-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 55%–84%, 30810 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 66% of hsa-miR-22-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 55%–84%, 30810 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_short: most common 3′ form −3 nt, 87% of reads (pooled) vs 0% with the miRBase end
three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-9985 in isomiRdb is −3 nt (87% of reads, pooled), against 0% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is not measured — no qPCR data exist for 3' end differences of 3 nt or more. The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 100% of hsa-miR-9985 reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 100%–100%, 301 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 100% of hsa-miR-9985 reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 100%–100%, 301 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -3.98 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [0.5, 10.5] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-19b-1-5p in isomiRdb is −1 nt (43.4% of reads, pooled), against 43.1% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 84% of hsa-miR-19b-1-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 34%–94%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 84% of hsa-miR-19b-1-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 34%–94%, 5317 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: These miRNAs cannot be distinguished by stem-loop RT-qPCR geometry alone: the RT overhang and the forward primer both fail to discriminate even at their length limits. Use a hydrolysis (TaqMan) probe spanning the differing region, an LNA-substituted primer, or an orthogonal method.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-6793-3p in isomiRdb is −1 nt (70% of reads, pooled), against 30% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 67% of hsa-miR-6793-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 0%–93%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 67% of hsa-miR-6793-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 0%–93%, 48 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 47% of hsa-let-7e-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 39%–55%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

sources.note: geNorm normalization strategy for miRNA qPCR
Selecting 3 most stable miRNAs by multiple algorithms for normalization
Reference miRNA selection depends on sample type

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -3.35 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [-7.8, 2.2] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 50% of hsa-miR-210-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 36%–73%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 60% of hsa-miR-450a-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 44%–77%, 18435 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 69% of hsa-miR-195-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 58%–79%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 69% of hsa-miR-195-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 58%–79%, 8073 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 69% of hsa-miR-195-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 58%–79%, 8073 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -5.47 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [11.1, 21.1] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 51% of hsa-miR-370-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 41%–67%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 51% of hsa-miR-370-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 41%–67%, 2019 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -2.95 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [-9.4, 0.6] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

specificity_warnings.data_note: Family data: miRBase CURRENT, seed-based grouping (positions 2-8). Overhang index: scripts/build_overhang_index.py (full per-species mature set). isoMiR data: curated from literature (8 entries, partial coverage). Re-run the build scripts after miRBase updates.

data_provenance.source: miRBase mature.fa (mature.fa, the file the BLAST DB was built from)

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 61% of hsa-miR-5000-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 48%–71%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 61% of hsa-miR-5000-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 48%–71%, 337 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 61% of hsa-miR-5000-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 48%–71%, 337 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_full_accuracy: informational (primer3, DNA:DNA NN; actual RT step involves DNA:RNA hybrid)

caveats: short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]
salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -4.9 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [5.8, 15.8] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 87% of hsa-miR-188-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 67%–95%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 87% of hsa-miR-188-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 67%–95%, 9285 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-6774-3p in isomiRdb is −2 nt then +G (88% of reads, pooled), against 12% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is not measured by qPCR. The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 83% of hsa-miR-6774-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 71%–87%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 83% of hsa-miR-6774-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 71%–87%, 468 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 83% of hsa-miR-6774-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 71%–87%, 468 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_short: most common 3′ form −1 nt, 59% of reads (pooled) vs 26% with the miRBase end
three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-450b-5p in isomiRdb is −1 nt (59% of reads, pooled), against 26% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 91% of hsa-miR-450b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 81%–96%, 19834 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 91% of hsa-miR-450b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 81%–96%, 19834 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -2.79 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [-13.5, -3.5] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-30c-5p in isomiRdb is +1 nt (51% of reads, pooled), against 27% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 71% of hsa-miR-30c-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 53%–86%). Fold-change caution: 71% of hsa-miR-30c-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 53%–86%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-30c-5p in isomiRdb is +1 nt (51% of reads, pooled), against 27% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.

protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels

Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 59% of hsa-miR-486-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 55%–66%, 40228 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-18b-5p in isomiRdb is −3 nt (39% of reads, pooled), against 28% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is not measured — no qPCR data exist for 3' end differences of 3 nt or more. The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 88% of hsa-miR-18b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 59%–96%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 88% of hsa-miR-18b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 59%–96%, 3941 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 88% of hsa-miR-18b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 59%–96%, 3941 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 63% of hsa-miR-6511a-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 57%–70%, 10636 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]

protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels

protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

specificity_warnings.data_note: Family data: miRBase CURRENT, seed-based grouping (positions 2-8). Overhang index: scripts/build_overhang_index.py (full per-species mature set). isoMiR data: curated from literature (8 entries, partial coverage). Re-run the build scripts after miRBase updates.

data_provenance.source: miRBase mature.fa (mature.fa, the file the BLAST DB was built from)

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_suggestion.note: A 7-nt RT overhang gives S2 level 5 (vs 4 with 6 nt) for the #1 set's 13-nt specific region. Suggestion only — the design was not changed. Off-label: only 6 nt was validated by Chen et al. 2005; not verified by wet-lab experiment.

probe.disclaimer: Probe Tm calculated at 1.5 mM Mg²⁺, 50.0 mM Na⁺ (primer3-py SantaLucia 1998). Actual Tm may differ if master-mix Mg²⁺ varies. Verify empirically before use.
warnings: Probe (27 nt) may not fit within the amplicon (~65 nt) alongside forward (21 nt) and universal reverse (20 nt) primers. Consider a shorter MGB probe or universal mode [RESEARCH_INSIGHTS_probe §2.3].

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_short: most common 3′ form +1 nt, 49% of reads (pooled) vs 15% with the miRBase end
three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-31-5p in isomiRdb is +1 nt (49% of reads, pooled), against 15% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 85% of hsa-miR-31-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 75%–92%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 85% of hsa-miR-31-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 75%–92%, 16841 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 85% of hsa-miR-31-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 75%–92%, 16841 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 54% of hsa-miR-3928-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 22%–75%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 54% of hsa-miR-3928-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 22%–75%, 2393 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

fwd.basis: 2 mismatches in the last 5 nt, terminal T (T–G) still extends [Kwok90]; duplex 31.3 °C weaker than on target

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is not measured (non-templated addition); if it behaves like a templated extension of the same length, captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 75% of hsa-miR-652-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 61%–88%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 75% of hsa-miR-652-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 61%–88%, 40550 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 75% of hsa-miR-652-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 61%–88%, 40550 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.
