three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 53% of hsa-miR-4446-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 39%–67%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 53% of hsa-miR-4446-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 39%–67%, 5567 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 53% of hsa-miR-4446-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 39%–67%, 5567 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -4.96 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [6.2, 16.2] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]

protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-548u in isomiRdb is −1 nt (52% of reads, pooled), against 33% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 66% of hsa-miR-548u reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 51%–84%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 66% of hsa-miR-548u reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 51%–84%, 470 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 66% of hsa-miR-548u reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 51%–84%, 470 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-122b-5p in isomiRdb is −1 nt (66% of reads, pooled), against 28% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 89% of hsa-miR-122b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 80%–95%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 89% of hsa-miR-122b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 80%–95%, 421 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_short: most common 3′ form +1 nt, 55% of reads (pooled) vs 26% with the miRBase end
three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-195-5p in isomiRdb is +1 nt (55% of reads, pooled), against 26% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 83% of hsa-miR-195-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 66%–89%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 83% of hsa-miR-195-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 66%–89%, 25317 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 83% of hsa-miR-195-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 66%–89%, 25317 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -5.37 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [11.8, 21.8] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 76% of hsa-miR-552-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 65%–88%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 76% of hsa-miR-552-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 65%–88%, 2267 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 76% of hsa-miR-552-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 65%–88%, 2267 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_short: most common 3′ form +4 nt, 32% of reads (pooled) vs 7% with the miRBase end
three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-4326 in isomiRdb is +4 nt (32% of reads, pooled), against 7% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is not measured — no qPCR data exist for 3' end differences of 3 nt or more. The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 99% of hsa-miR-4326 reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 93%–100%, 14761 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 99% of hsa-miR-4326 reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 93%–100%, 14761 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -3.62 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [-4.1, 5.9] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-345-5p in isomiRdb is −1 nt (37% of reads, pooled), against 32% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 75% of hsa-miR-345-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 63%–88%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 75% of hsa-miR-345-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 63%–88%, 36440 human samples).

The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -6.86 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [20.9, 30.9] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

warnings.message: In isomiRdb, a median 75% of hsa-miR-345-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 63%–88%, 36440 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

Fold-change caution: 75% of hsa-miR-345-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 63%–88%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-345-5p in isomiRdb is −1 nt (37% of reads, pooled), against 32% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: These miRNAs cannot be distinguished by stem-loop RT-qPCR geometry alone: the RT overhang and the forward primer both fail to discriminate even at their length limits. Use a hydrolysis (TaqMan) probe spanning the differing region, an LNA-substituted primer, or an orthogonal method.

The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 100% of hsa-miR-548ay-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 100%–100%, 122 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]

protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 81% of hsa-miR-488-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 0%–93%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 81% of hsa-miR-488-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 0%–93%, 1185 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

warnings.message: In isomiRdb, a median 81% of hsa-miR-488-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 0%–93%, 1185 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

Fold-change caution: 81% of hsa-miR-488-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 0%–93%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -4.93 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [7.4, 17.4] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-190a-5p in isomiRdb is +1 nt (35% of reads, pooled), against 22% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 83% of hsa-miR-190a-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 69%–92%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 83% of hsa-miR-190a-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 69%–92%, 13305 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 83% of hsa-miR-190a-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 69%–92%, 13305 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels

Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 28% of hsa-let-7a-2-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 18%–40%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 28% of hsa-let-7a-2-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 18%–40%, 3855 human samples).

salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -3.39 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [-5.4, 4.6] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 67% of hsa-miR-17-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 22%–86%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 67% of hsa-miR-17-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 22%–86%, 34347 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 60% of hsa-miR-1260b reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 51%–73%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 60% of hsa-miR-1260b reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 51%–73%, 22414 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 60% of hsa-miR-1260b reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 51%–73%, 22414 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_full_accuracy: informational (primer3, DNA:DNA NN; actual RT step involves DNA:RNA hybrid)

caveats: short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]
salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -3.58 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [-4.1, 5.9] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

Reference miRNA selection depends on sample type

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 77% of hsa-miR-100-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 53%–92%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 77% of hsa-miR-100-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 53%–92%, 38226 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 77% of hsa-miR-100-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 53%–92%, 38226 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -4.52 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [4.6, 14.6] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

warnings.message: Fold-change caution: 41% of hsa-miR-299-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 27%–52%). overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 63% of hsa-miR-708-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 55%–71%, 20653 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

sources.note: geNorm normalization strategy for miRNA qPCR

Reference miRNA selection depends on sample type

specificity_warnings.data_note: Family data: miRBase CURRENT, seed-based grouping (positions 2-8). Overhang index: scripts/build_overhang_index.py (full per-species mature set). isoMiR data: curated from literature (8 entries, partial coverage). Re-run the build scripts after miRBase updates.

data_provenance.source: miRBase mature.fa (mature.fa, the file the BLAST DB was built from)

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

three_prime_isomir.data_warning: Human miRNAs in isomiRdb only. Absence of an entry means no data, not absence of 3' isomiRs.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 56% of hsa-miR-181b-2-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 46%–65%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 56% of hsa-miR-181b-2-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 46%–65%, 1442 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 56% of hsa-miR-181b-2-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 46%–65%, 1442 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_full_accuracy: informational (primer3, DNA:DNA NN; actual RT step involves DNA:RNA hybrid)

caveats: short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]
salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -4.6 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [4.7, 14.7] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: These miRNAs cannot be distinguished by stem-loop RT-qPCR geometry alone: the RT overhang and the forward primer both fail to discriminate even at their length limits. Use a hydrolysis (TaqMan) probe spanning the differing region, an LNA-substituted primer, or an orthogonal method.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

three_prime_isomir.data_warning: Human miRNAs in isomiRdb only. Absence of an entry means no data, not absence of 3' isomiRs.
three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_short: most common 3′ form +1 nt, 89% of reads (pooled) vs 11% with the miRBase end
three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-302b-5p in isomiRdb is +1 nt (89% of reads, pooled), against 11% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 80% of hsa-miR-302b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 0%–89%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 80% of hsa-miR-302b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 0%–89%, 781 human samples).
three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 80% of hsa-miR-302b-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 0%–89%, 781 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -4.66 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [5.7, 15.7] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

Selecting 3 most stable miRNAs by multiple algorithms for normalization
Reference miRNA selection depends on sample type

fwd.basis: mismatch 5 nt from the 3′ end; duplex 29.3 °C weaker than on target

data_provenance.source: miRBase mature.fa (mature.fa, the file the BLAST DB was built from)

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

recommendation.reason: No other miRNA is predicted to co-amplify (ΔCq_assay ≥ 3.3 for all).

three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 28% of hsa-miR-664b-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 14%–41%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.
three_prime_isomir.summary: In isomiRdb, a median 28% of hsa-miR-664b-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 14%–41%, 3226 human samples).

caveats: short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]
salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

stemloop_rt.tm_note: RT overhang is 6 nt (< 8 bp): a point Tm is not reportable — nearest-neighbour initiation and terminal fraying dominate at this length. Reported instead: ΔG37 = -3.95 kcal/mol (Sugimoto 1995 DNA:RNA NN, 4 μM, 75 mM KCl) and an indicative Tm band [-1.9, 8.1] (± 5 °C, not a statistical CI). Use ΔG37 for relative ranking, not the Tm as an absolute value. short-duplex NN extrapolation (4–8 bp): uncertainty ±3–5°C [Sugimoto95 range]; salt correction for DNA:RNA is approximate (SantaLucia 1998 monovalent formula) [SL98]

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-511-3p in isomiRdb is +2 nt (40% of reads, pooled), against 20% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.
three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 67% of hsa-miR-511-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 41%–84%). Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 67% of hsa-miR-511-3p reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 41%–84%, 1940 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

Stem-loop RT-qPCR captures 3' isoforms selectively by length, so if a treatment, infection or disease state shifts the isoform mix, the measured fold change mixes that shift with the real change in miRNA level — Nejad et al. 2018 showed exactly this for miR-222-3p under IFN-β and for >40 miRNA families after Salmonella infection, and warned it 'can lead to misinterpretation of results'. Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-511-3p in isomiRdb is +2 nt (40% of reads, pooled), against 20% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. RNA 2019;25(2):232–238, PMID 30487268]. isomiRdb pools all sample types, so the isoform mix in your samples may differ.

pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

Reference miRNA selection depends on sample type

fwd.basis: 2 mismatches in the last 5 nt, terminal T (T–G) still extends [Kwok90]; duplex 57.3 °C weaker than on target

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 3–4 Ct later than the reference form (one miRNA measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 69% of hsa-miR-128-1-5p reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 54%–84%). Keep the comparison qualitative, or confirm a surprising fold change by small RNA sequencing.

The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use
protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization requires no prior gene selection — suitable for panels >10 targets [Hacimoto24]
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
protocol_advice.recommendation: Use geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 housekeeping gene. For panels ≥10 targets, global-mean normalization avoids needing candidate reference genes. Reference stability is sample-type dependent (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.

three_prime_isomir.dominant_isoform_warning: Dominant 3' isoform: the most common 3' form of hsa-miR-9902 in isomiRdb is −1 nt (58% of reads, pooled), against 37% (pooled) with the miRBase 22.1 3' end. The RT primer's 6-nt overhang pairs with the miRBase 22.1 3' end; this isoform is captured 0–4 Ct later than the reference form (two miRNAs measured). The measured value can therefore follow the reference form more than the dominant one: if the isoform mix differs between groups, the fold change can be wrong, even in direction — Pillman et al. 2019 found this for miR-221-3p and miR-27b-3p in stimulated macrophages with stem-loop TaqMan assays [Pillman KA et al. three_prime_isomir.fold_change_bias_warning: Fold-change caution: 64% of hsa-miR-9902 reads are 3'-end isoforms and that share itself swings between samples (IQR 55%–73%). three_prime_isomir.warning: In isomiRdb, a median 64% of hsa-miR-9902 reads are 3'-end isoforms (IQR 55%–73%, 1752 human samples). The stem-loop RT primer pairs with the canonical 3'-terminal 6 nt, yet variants 1 nt shorter or 1–2 nt longer are detected 0–4 Ct later (two miRNAs measured) and 2-nt-shorter ones 3–4 Ct later (one miRNA measured) [Schamberger14]. The signal is therefore a capture-weighted sum of 3' isoforms, not the canonical form alone — here the canonical form is a minority. Report the result as the sum of isoforms [Magee17]; isoform-resolved quantification needs sequencing.

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels

protocol_advice.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder identifies stable references from a panel, reducing systematic bias [Hellemans14]

overhang_collision.interpretation: An off-target gives signal only if the RT overhang captures it AND the forward primer primes its cDNA; the delays add (ΔCq_assay ≈ ΔCq_RT + ΔCq_FWD, cross-reactivity ≈ 2^−ΔCq). Values are lower bounds of published data (Chen 2005, Czimmerer 2013, Schamberger 2014, Stadhouders 2010) measured with TaqMan probes; for SYBR the prediction is optimistic. miRBase entries carrying the same sequence, or one shifted ≤ 2 nt at an end (synonyms, paralogues), cannot be separated by any primer design and are listed apart (Magee 2017). Biological isomiRs have no miRBase entries and are covered by the RT-primer isomiR flags. Seed-family membership is reported for context only.
